title: Stress-enhanced diffusion in Yukawa crystals
summary: Self-diffusion in crystallized Coulomb (Yukawa) plasmas proceeds by the thermally activated formation of vacancy-interstitial pairs and the migration of these defects through the lattice, commonly known as Frenkel pairs in the materials literature. Molecular dynamics has recently resolved an Eyring law for diffusion in unstrained crystals, which we generalize to deformed crystals in this work. We simulate sheared Yukawa crystals and show that a static elastic strain exponentially enhances diffusion due to the additional elastic energy stored in the region that participates in Frenkel pair formation relative to the unstrained crystal: $D(\varepsilon)=D_0(Γ^{*})\exp[V^{*}σ/k_{\rm B}T]$, with $σ=\tfrac12μ\varepsilon^{2}$ the elastic energy density stored by the shear strain $\varepsilon$ and $V^{*}$ the activation volume. We find a single activation volume $N_{\rm act} = n_iV^{*}\simeq31$ suffices for typical astrophysical screenings with a reduction at higher screening. This suggests Frenkel pair formation requires only a brief coordination of the nearest neighbors at a thermal maximum in oscillation. Stress-enhanced diffusion supplies a microphysical mechanism for creep in strained neutron star crusts and crystallizing white dwarf cores.

AI.tldr: Molecular dynamics simulations of sheared Yukawa (Coulomb) crystals generalize the Eyring diffusion law to deformed crystals. A static elastic shear strain exponentially enhances self-diffusion through Frenkel-pair formation, following D(ε)=D0(Γ*) exp[V*σ/(k_B T)] with σ=(1/2)μ ε^2. A single activation volume N_act=n_i V*≈31 suffices for typical astrophysical screenings, with a reduction at higher screening, suggesting stress-enhanced diffusion as a microphysical creep mechanism in neutron star crusts and crystallizing white dwarf cores.
AI.motivation: The paper aims to understand self-diffusion in crystallized Coulomb (Yukawa) plasmas under deformation, generalizing the recently resolved Eyring law for unstrained crystals to strained crystals. It also seeks a microphysical mechanism for creep in strained neutron star crusts and crystallizing white dwarf cores.
AI.method: The authors perform molecular dynamics simulations of sheared Yukawa crystals and analyze diffusion as thermally activated vacancy-interstitial (Frenkel pair) formation and defect migration. They express the strain effect through the stored elastic energy density σ=(1/2)μ ε^2 and an activation volume V*, obtaining D(ε)=D0(Γ*) exp[V*σ/(k_B T)], and they examine the activation volume N_act=n_i V* across astrophysical screening conditions.
AI.result: Static elastic strain exponentially enhances diffusion relative to unstrained crystals. The diffusion coefficient follows D(ε)=D0(Γ*) exp[V*σ/(k_B T)], where σ is the elastic energy density stored by shear strain ε and V* is the activation volume. A single activation volume N_act=n_i V*≈31 suffices for typical astrophysical screenings, with a reduction at higher screening. The results suggest Frenkel pair formation requires only brief nearest-neighbor coordination at a thermal maximum in oscillation.
AI.conclusion: Stress-enhanced diffusion provides a microphysical mechanism for creep in strained neutron star crusts and crystallizing white dwarf cores. The approximately common activation volume for typical astrophysical screenings, with reduction at higher screening, supports the proposed strain-dependent Frenkel-pair diffusion picture. Quantitative creep rates and experimental validation are not provided in the abstract.

title: As a matter of reconstruction -- varying the magnetic Prandtl number in implicit large eddy simulations
summary: The magnetic Prandtl number ($\mathrm{Pm}$), the ratio of viscosity to magnetic diffusivity, spans many orders of magnitude in astrophysical plasmas. It shapes how turbulence amplifies and structures magnetic fields. In direct numerical simulations (DNS) the viscosity and magnetic diffusivity can be controlled explicitly and independently, whereas in implicit large eddy simulations (ILES) they are set by the numerical scheme. We test whether, in a finite-volume code, $\mathrm{Pm}$ can be varied through the reconstruction scheme by applying different methods to the hydro and magnetic variables. As a proof of concept, we simulate driven, subsonic, homogeneous magnetohydrodynamic turbulence using five pairs of hydrodynamic and magnetic reconstruction schemes at varying resolutions. We measure the effective viscosity and resistivity from the energy transfer between scales. Reconstructing the magnetic field at higher order than the fluid raises the effective magnetic Prandtl number and vice versa. We demonstrate that a mix of second- and third-order reconstruction alone results in a $\gtrsim20\times$ change in $\mathrm{Pm}$. A comparison of DNS with matched explicit dissipation at these values agrees with the ILES. Mixed reconstruction thus offers a simple and efficient way to explore $\mathrm{Pm} \not\simeq 1$ in ILES without adding explicit dissipation.

AI.tldr: The paper tests whether the effective magnetic Prandtl number in finite-volume implicit large eddy simulations can be controlled by using different reconstruction orders for hydrodynamic and magnetic variables. Five reconstruction-scheme pairs are tested on driven, subsonic, homogeneous magnetohydrodynamic turbulence, with effective viscosity and resistivity measured from inter-scale energy transfer. Mixed reconstruction changes Pm by more than 20x and agrees with matched-dissipation DNS.
AI.motivation: The magnetic Prandtl number spans many orders of magnitude in astrophysical plasmas and shapes how turbulence amplifies and structures magnetic fields. DNS can set viscosity and magnetic diffusivity independently, but ILES have them determined by the numerical scheme, so a simple way to vary Pm in ILES is needed.
AI.method: The authors use a finite-volume code to simulate driven, subsonic, homogeneous magnetohydrodynamic turbulence with five pairs of hydrodynamic and magnetic reconstruction schemes at varying resolutions. They measure effective viscosity and resistivity from energy transfer between scales and compare ILES results with DNS using matched explicit dissipation.
AI.result: Reconstructing the magnetic field at higher order than the fluid increases the effective magnetic Prandtl number, and the reverse decreases it. A mix of second- and third-order reconstruction alone produces a change in Pm of at least about 20x. DNS with matched explicit dissipation at these values agrees with the ILES.
AI.conclusion: Mixed reconstruction provides a simple and efficient way to explore Pm not equal to 1 in ILES without adding explicit dissipation.

title: From proof of concept to practice: the next decade of artificial intelligence in metasurface photonics
comment: 33 pages main text plus 13 pages of Supplementary Information
summary: Over the past decade, artificial intelligence has learned to predict electromagnetic responses rapidly and generate high-performance metasurface designs. However, one question remains open: compared with conventional design workflows that contain no learned model, has it made the complete design workflow faster, and are the resulting devices better? We argue that the answer depends on the task. Reading 100 highly cited optical studies in depth, we distinguish the design tasks in which artificial intelligence is irreplaceable, clearly advantageous, or without clear advantage. In our view, the key to the next decade is not more successes in isolated tasks but making each success a foundation for the field, through shifts such as shared data, trained models, and physics written into learning. Whether artificial intelligence leaves lasting value in this field will depend on whether its benefits can be verified, its methods transferred, and its designs corrected by experiment.

AI.tldr: This perspective examines whether AI actually speeds up the complete metasurface design workflow and yields better devices than conventional workflows, concluding that the answer is task-dependent based on an in-depth reading of 100 highly cited optical studies.
AI.motivation: The paper addresses the open question of whether AI, despite rapidly predicting electromagnetic responses and generating high-performance metasurface designs, improves the complete design workflow and produces better devices compared with conventional design workflows that contain no learned model.
AI.method: The authors perform an in-depth reading of 100 highly cited optical studies and categorize design tasks according to whether AI is irreplaceable, clearly advantageous, or without clear advantage. The abstract does not provide quantitative comparisons or specific task-level details.
AI.result: The authors argue that AI's advantage depends on the task. They identify three categories of design tasks: those where AI is irreplaceable, those where it is clearly advantageous, and those where it has no clear advantage. The abstract does not report specific performance metrics or device outcomes.
AI.conclusion: The key to the next decade is not more isolated task successes but making each success a foundation for the field through shared data, trained models, and physics written into learning. AI's lasting value will depend on whether its benefits can be verified, its methods transferred, and its designs corrected by experiment.

title: Decay of space plasma turbulence downstream of bow shocks: MMS magnetosheath unbiased campaign observations
summary: Turbulence properties in the solar wind change with increasing heliospheric distance. Observations from different missions have shown how spectral indices converge towards a $f^{-5/3}$ spectrum in the inertial range as the solar wind reaches one astronomical unit, and how the cascade rate decays as the plasma moves away from the Sun. We evaluate whether these properties display similar trends in a smaller astrophysical system, that of a planetary magnetosheath. Using data from the 2023 Magnetospheric Multiscale (MMS) unbiased magnetosheath campaign, we determine the evolution of the spectral indices and the cascade rate along 15 inbound magnetosheath crossings. WIND observations permitted to monitor the state of the solar wind during the campaign and allowed to study the impact of the upstream plasma conditions on the evolution of the cascade rate downstream the bow shock. Our results show an increase of the cascade rate between two to three orders of magnitude after the plasma crosses the bow shock into the magnetosheath. Once in the magnetosheath, turbulence develops with increasing distance to the bow shock in a way similar to solar wind observations, despite the smaller size of the system. Incompressible Hall-MHD scaling-law estimates of the cascade rate show a clear power-law decay of the cascade rate in the magnetosheath, particularly for the cases with upstream slow wind. This suggests that the way energy is injected into the system plays a role in the decay of turbulence as the plasma moves away from the bow shock.

AI.tldr: Using MMS magnetosheath crossings and WIND solar-wind monitoring, the study finds that turbulence cascade rates rise by two to three orders of magnitude across the bow shock and then decay with distance in the magnetosheath, similar to solar-wind trends despite the smaller system size.
AI.motivation: The paper evaluates whether turbulence trends observed in the solar wind—spectral indices converging toward f^-5/3 in the inertial range and cascade rate decaying with heliospheric distance—also appear in a smaller astrophysical system, the planetary magnetosheath, and whether upstream solar-wind conditions affect cascade-rate evolution downstream of the bow shock.
AI.method: The authors use data from the 2023 Magnetospheric Multiscale (MMS) unbiased magnetosheath campaign to track spectral indices and cascade rates along 15 inbound magnetosheath crossings. WIND observations monitor the solar wind during the campaign and are used to assess upstream plasma conditions. Incompressible Hall-MHD scaling-law estimates are used for cascade-rate calculations.
AI.result: The cascade rate increases by two to three orders of magnitude after plasma crosses the bow shock into the magnetosheath. Within the magnetosheath, turbulence develops with increasing distance from the bow shock in a manner similar to solar-wind observations despite the smaller system size. Incompressible Hall-MHD scaling-law estimates show a clear power-law decay of cascade rate in the magnetosheath, particularly for cases with upstream slow wind.
AI.conclusion: The results suggest that the manner in which energy is injected into the system plays a role in the decay of turbulence as plasma moves away from the bow shock.

title: Chirality inversion and odd transport in a suspension of living rotors
summary: Chiral symmetry breaking is a defining feature of life, visible at all scales from molecules to organisms. Yet how microscopic chirality propagates to shape the macroscopic properties of living matter remains poorly understood. Here, using a new experimental system of spinning microalgae, we show that a living chiral fluid behaves fundamentally differently from an externally driven one. As their density increases, cells self-assemble hydrodynamically into small rotating clusters which merge into a percolating chiral fluid. Strikingly, microscopic and macroscopic vorticity have opposite signs: individual cells all spin clockwise, yet clusters orbit counterclockwise. Combining experiments, theory and simulations, we show that both chirality inversion and percolation are direct consequences of the cells' internally driven nature. We then show how percolation reshapes transport, with even and odd diffusivities responding differently to the emerging network topology.

AI.tldr: Using spinning microalgae, the paper shows that a living chiral fluid self-organizes into rotating clusters and a percolating network, with microscopic clockwise cell spinning producing counterclockwise cluster orbits; theory and simulations attribute chirality inversion and percolation to internal activity, and percolation alters even and odd diffusivities.
AI.motivation: Chiral symmetry breaking is ubiquitous in life, but how microscopic chirality propagates to macroscopic properties of living matter is poorly understood. The paper aims to clarify the collective behavior of a living chiral fluid and distinguish it from externally driven chiral systems.
AI.method: The authors introduce a new experimental system of spinning microalgae and combine experiments, theory, and simulations. They vary cell density to study self-assembly, cluster formation, percolation, vorticity, and transport, including even and odd diffusivities.
AI.result: As density increases, cells hydrodynamically self-assemble into small rotating clusters that merge into a percolating chiral fluid. Individual cells spin clockwise, while clusters orbit counterclockwise. Experiments, theory, and simulations indicate that both chirality inversion and percolation arise from the cells' internally driven nature. Percolation reshapes transport, with even and odd diffusivities responding differently to the emerging network topology.
AI.conclusion: A living chiral fluid behaves fundamentally differently from an externally driven chiral fluid. Internal activity drives chirality inversion and percolation, and the resulting network topology modifies transport; the abstract does not provide specific quantitative metrics.

title: Microscopic Theory of Spin-Orbit Interactions of Light
summary: Optical spin-orbit interactions (SOI), demonstrated experimentally in optical cavities, enable the polarization degrees of freedom of light to be described and controlled as an effective pseudospin, providing a foundation for spintronic-like control of light and the development of next-generation optical technologies. However, prior works describe this emergent effect using phenomenological models that fail to uncover its microscopic quantum origins, and as a result, a rigorous connection between material electronic structure and the optical SOI remains elusive. In this work, we address this fundamental challenge by developing a microscopic quantum theory starting from the non-relativistic quantum electrodynamical (QED) description of light-matter interactions. We show that this effect arises from virtual interactions between confined photons and material excitations. Crucially, our theoretical framework provides microscopic material-design principles for tuning the distinct components of optical SOI, which include the optical birefringence, photonic self-energies, TE-TM splitting, and optical Zeeman splitting, enabling precise engineering of effective magnetic fields, diabolical points, and pseudospin textures. We anticipate that the predictive capability of our microscopic theory will enable systematic screening and design of material systems for photonic spintronics and optical technologies.

AI.tldr: The paper develops a microscopic quantum theory based on non-relativistic QED showing that optical spin-orbit interactions arise from virtual interactions between confined photons and material excitations, thereby linking material electronic structure to optical SOI and providing principles for tuning its components and engineering pseudospin-related phenomena.
AI.motivation: Previous descriptions of optical SOI in optical cavities relied on phenomenological models that did not reveal the effect's microscopic quantum origins, leaving a rigorous connection between material electronic structure and optical SOI elusive. Establishing this connection is important for controlling light via an effective pseudospin and for photonic spintronics and next-generation optical technologies.
AI.method: The authors develop a microscopic quantum theory starting from the non-relativistic quantum electrodynamical description of light-matter interactions. They show that optical SOI arises from virtual interactions between confined photons and material excitations.
AI.result: The framework provides microscopic material-design principles for tuning distinct optical SOI components, including optical birefringence, photonic self-energies, TE-TM splitting, and optical Zeeman splitting. It enables precise engineering of effective magnetic fields, diabolical points, and pseudospin textures. The abstract does not provide quantitative results or experimental validation.
AI.conclusion: The authors conclude that their microscopic theory's predictive capability could enable systematic screening and design of material systems for photonic spintronics and optical technologies.

title: Spectroscopic observations of periodic bursty ejections during a dome-spire-shaped jet
summary:
Context: The study investigates the complexity of the formation and evolution of a dome-spire-shaped jet (or anemone jet) that originated in an active region and was presumably driven by null-point magnetic reconnection.
  Aims: We aim to provide a quantitative estimation of multi-temperature plasma dynamics and physical parameters of the jet and its blob-like features, together with its temporal evolution in three-dimensional perspective.
  Methods: For this, we analyze unique sit-and-stare spectral (Si IV, Mg II k, and C II) and slit-jaw imaging 1400 Å and 2796 Å observations obtained with the Interface Region Imaging Spectrograph (IRIS), with a slit uniquely positioned just above the assumed reconnection site. Co-observations taken with the Fast Imaging Solar Spectrograph of the Goode Solar Telescope in the chromospheric H$α$ and Ca II 8542.10 Å lines were also analyzed. These data are complemented by EUV imaging information from the Atmospheric Imaging Assembly on board the Solar Dynamics Observatory.
  Results: The IRIS observations reveal that the jet is formed by multiple periodic ($\sim$30 s) plasma ejections with blob-like appearance, each associated with strongly blueshifted Si IV 1402.77 Å transition-region emission reaching about $-300$ km/s. More importantly, the ejections are grouped into well-defined packets, each lasting approximately 3--5 min. In contrast, only a single Doppler component is observed in the chromospheric Ca II line. Multi-Gaussian decomposition of the Si IV line profiles reveals a highly accelerated plasma, with line-of-sight speed toward the observer increasing linearly from $\sim$30 to 112 km/s over 66 s, corresponding to an acceleration of 1.3 km/s$^2$. The kinetic energy release rate is estimated in the range of $\sim$1.0$\times10^{24}$--1.0$\times10^{25}$ erg\,s$^{-1}$.

The ejections are grouped into well-defined packets lasting approximately 3–5 min. Only a single Doppler component is observed in the chromospheric Ca II line. Multi-Gaussian decomposition of Si IV profiles reveals highly accelerated plasma, with line-of-sight speed toward the observer increasing linearly from ~30 to 112 km/s over 66 s, corresponding to an acceleration of 1.3 km/s^2. title: Nonlinear visco-elasto-plastic model for the stress-strain and stress-relaxation in metallic glass
summary: We develop a nonlinear visco-elasto-plastic (VEP) model for the stress-strain response of metallic glasses by connecting the deformation dynamics with the material relaxation time obtained from independent stress-relaxation measurements. The material is modeled as a Maxwell-type element, with a nonlinear elastic spring and a stretched-exponential dashpot whose behavior is determined from the separate stress-relaxation data. The model captures the effects of temperature and strain rate on the initial elastic response, stress overshoot, post-yield softening, and steady flow. We independently determine the reference material-time function $X_0(\varepsilon)$ from the stress-relaxation response and the nonlinear material-time variable $X(\varepsilon)$ from the elastic-viscoplastic strain decomposition based on the stress-strain response. We introduce an Eyring-type function or material-time ratio $φ(\varepsilon)=X(\varepsilon)/X_0(\varepsilon)$ which quantifies the change of relaxation dynamics during nonlinear deformation. Our model provides a simple connection between structural relaxation and yielding in metallic glasses.

AI.tldr: The paper develops a nonlinear visco-elasto-plastic model for metallic glasses that links stress-strain deformation to independently measured stress-relaxation dynamics via a Maxwell-type nonlinear elastic spring and stretched-exponential dashpot. It captures temperature- and strain-rate-dependent elastic response, overshoot, softening, and steady flow, and defines a material-time ratio to quantify changes in relaxation dynamics during nonlinear deformation.
AI.motivation: The work aims to connect the deformation dynamics of metallic glasses with their material relaxation time obtained from independent stress-relaxation measurements, thereby providing a simple link between structural relaxation and yielding.
AI.method: The material is modeled as a Maxwell-type element combining a nonlinear elastic spring and a stretched-exponential dashpot whose behavior is determined from separate stress-relaxation data. The reference material-time function X0(epsilon) is independently determined from stress-relaxation response, while the nonlinear material-time variable X(epsilon) is obtained from elastic-viscoplastic strain decomposition based on the stress-strain response. An Eyring-type material-time ratio phi(epsilon)=X(epsilon)/X0(epsilon) is introduced to quantify changes in relaxation dynamics during nonlinear deformation.

AI.conclusion: The proposed nonlinear visco-elasto-plastic model provides a simple connection between structural relaxation and yielding in metallic glasses through the material-time ratio and independently determined relaxation dynamics.

title: Comparison of melanin subtypes using pump-probe microscopy
summary: Pump-probe microscopy (PPM) is used to probe excited state dynamics of endogenous chromophores to generate contrast that is unavailable in traditional forms of microscopy. Here we apply PPM to characterize melanin, a pigment central to photoprotection, skin and eye pigmentation, and melanoma pathogenesis. Melanin is notoriously difficult to analyze due to its structural and chemical complexity. We imaged melanin from six different lesion categories: cutaneous nevi, lentigo, cutaneous malignant melanoma, conjunctival melanocytic lesions, vulvar melanocytic lesions, and a murine melanoma model, across 21 independent biological samples and 109 regions of interest. Using model fitting, adapted phasor analysis, and support vector machine classification, we characterize and quantify excited-state dynamics as a surrogate for chemical and structural heterogeneity. Heterogeneity of melanin separates cutaneous from non-cutaneous lesions, but is not correlated with malignancy. Benign lentigo is the most heterogeneous population in the dataset, exceeding cutaneous malignant melanoma, while conjunctival lesions are the most homogeneous despite receiving direct solar exposure. Classification on full transient absorption curves separates most subtypes well above the six-class chance level. These findings demonstrate the ability of PPM to reveal subtle differences in melanin photophysics across diverse tissue environments, with implications for optical tissue classification and the understanding of melanoma pathogenesis.

AI.tldr: Pump-probe microscopy characterizes melanin excited-state dynamics across diverse melanocytic lesions, revealing heterogeneity differences and enabling subtype classification.
AI.motivation: Pump-probe microscopy can probe endogenous chromophore excited-state dynamics to provide contrast unavailable in traditional microscopy, and melanin is difficult to analyze because of its structural and chemical complexity.
AI.method: The authors used pump-probe microscopy to image melanin from six lesion categories across 21 independent biological samples and 109 regions of interest, applying model fitting, adapted phasor analysis, and support vector machine classification to excited-state dynamics as a surrogate for chemical and structural heterogeneity; classification was also performed on full transient absorption curves.
AI.result: Melanin heterogeneity separated cutaneous from non-cutaneous lesions but was not correlated with malignancy. Benign lentigo was the most heterogeneous population, exceeding cutaneous malignant melanoma, while conjunctival lesions were the most homogeneous despite direct solar exposure. Classification on full transient absorption curves separated most subtypes well above the six-class chance level.

title: Subsonic terahertz plasmon instability in space-time plasmonic crystals

summary: We investigate collective plasma-wave dynamics in a two-dimensional electron fluid subected to a travelling periodic modulation of the effective plasma velocity. title: Frozen in Time: How a Physics Foundation Model Forgets Under Sim-to-Real Adaptation
comment: Accepted at the Sim2Science workshop, NeurIPS 2026. Code: https://github.com/haarisamian/walrus-forgetting-paper
summary: Scientific foundation models (SciFMs) have achieved remarkable performance on a wide range of PDEs, including the ability to efficiently adapt to unseen data distributions with additional finetuning. We study catastrophic forgetting in Walrus-1.3B, a SciFM for continuum dynamics, over the course of a two-stage sim-to-real adaptation: first finetuning on simulated flow around a cylinder and then adapting to experimental data of the same system. We find that finetuning on the simulations rapidly degrades rollout performance on the original pretraining datasets, with one-step errors increasing up to 35x after just 20 epochs. Subsequent adaptation to real data further erodes performance on the simulated task. We characterize the potential drivers of forgetting, such as dataset dependence and task representation similarity. We then show that replaying as little as 1% simulated data during real-data finetuning recovers most of the lost simulation performance while retaining effective adaptation to the experimental dynamics. Our results identify catastrophic forgetting as a practical obstacle to sim-to-real adaptation of SciFMs and show that lightweight replay strategies significantly improve retention.

title: Metadevices that compute: mathematical foundations and experimental implementations for neuromorphic nanophotonics
comment: 37 pages, 7 figures, 2 tables. Review article submitted to npj Nanophotonics
summary: Wave-based analog computing has re-emerged as a compelling alternative to digital electronics for specific linear-algebraic and machine-learning workloads, promising massively parallel, high-bandwidth, and energy-efficient information processing. Metamaterials, metasurfaces, and integrated metastructures (collectively, metadevices) now perform mathematical operations, solve integral and differential equations, multiply matrices, and implement trainable photonic neural networks directly in the wave domain. We conclude with open problems and opportunities for this emerging neuromorphic nanophotonics ecosystem.

title: Learning Nonlocal Interactions in Large-Scale Heterogeneous Metamaterials through Scientific Machine Learning
summary: In multiscale systems, nonlocal interactions among spatially distributed constituents can unlock collective, potentially emergent behavior irreducible to individual constituent responses. Beyond characterization, nonlocality in multiscale systems is increasingly viewed as a design element across fracture mechanics, wave physics, and disordered systems. Existing nonlocality theories provide rigorous descriptions and mechanistic insight, but often require prescribed analytic forms, range, symmetries, or periodicity. Machine learning offers a data-driven route to learn interactions, yet principled approaches that tie the network design to physical theory remain nascent. Here we present domain-decomposition attention neural operator (DANO), which learns configuration-dependent interactions in heterogeneous systems governed by linear field equations from field data alone. Through a case study in large-scale optical metasurfaces, we demonstrate DANO's full-field prediction under geometric heterogeneity and across drive conditions, small-to-large domain transfer, and multifunctional inverse design, with learned interactions validated through physics-based interrogation. As an AI-for-Science tool, it supports interaction discovery and scalable, customizable design of nonlocal multiscale systems, including virtual-reality optics.

title: Dipolar Exciton Polarons in a van der Waals Homobilayer
summary: Fermi polarons exemplify how many-body interactions give rise to emergent quasiparticles, providing a fundamental framework for understanding interacting quantum matter. In electron-doped two-dimensional semiconductors, exciton polarons offer optical access to Fermi-polaron physics and electrical tunability, yet achieving stronger and more controllable exciton-electron interactions remains a key challenge. Here, we realize dipolar exciton polarons in an electrically tunable van der Waals homobilayer, where interlayer excitons with spatially separated electrons and holes act as quantum impurities carrying permanent electric dipole moments. These dipolar polarons exhibit substantially enhanced exciton-electron interactions, with binding energies more than four times those of conventional intralayer exciton polarons. We further demonstrate that Fermi-sea layer polarization provides an additional degree of freedom for controlling many-body interactions. In particular, the presence of a Fermi sea induces hybridization between oppositely oriented dipolar polarons, whereas confining the Fermi sea to a single layer suppresses this hybridization and produces orientation-selective many-body dressing. Our findings establish an experimental platform for dipolar-polaron physics in which dipole orientation and Fermi-sea layer polarization jointly govern many-body interactions, opening a route towards electrically tunable interactions and dipolar-polaron-mediated attraction between itinerant electrons.

title: High-efficiency photonic GHZ measurements with linear optics
summary: Probabilistic and destructive Bell-measurements, also known as fusions, constitute a fundamental primitive for photonic quantum technologies. These operations rely only on pairwise photonic interference, whereas the computational power of photonic quantum systems originates from many-body interference. Here, we introduce a family of high-efficiency linear-optical GHZ measurements based on four-mode interferometers and show that incorporating many-body interference into this ubiquitous primitive leads to more efficient entangling operations. For the four-photon case, the success probability is $9/32$, and adaptive variants ensure that unsuccessful events project onto useful stabilizer states. We further show that the approach naturally generalizes to larger GHZ measurements, yielding an exponentially higher success probability than previous linear-optical schemes. Finally, we demonstrate practical advantages for graph-state resource generation, entanglement distribution between remote spin-photon interfaces, and fusion-based quantum computing. Our results establish high-efficiency many-body measurements as a new primitive for scalable photonic quantum information processing.

title: Cryogenic Optical Characteristics of S-FPL51 and S-LAH71: Refractive index, Transmission and Thermal expansion
comment: 15 pages, 6 tables, 11 figures. Submitted and presented at SPIE Astronomical Telescopes and Instrumentation 2024
summary:

title: Quantum Advantage in Beam-Displacement Estimation for Inter-Satellite Quantum-Secure Time Transfer
summary: In this work, we investigate the practical feasibility of achieving a quantum advantage, in the context of inter-satellite quantum communication, of satellite position estimation. title: Spectral Information Content of Diffraction-Limited Images
summary: High-resolution optical imaging is fundamentally limited by diffraction, which imprints wavelength-dependent structure onto the point spread function (PSF) of the optical system. This intrinsic chromaticity implies that in addition to spatial structure, images encode spectral information. We show that polychromatic PSF formation can be expressed as a convolution in logarithmic coordinates and define the corresponding spectral transfer function. We derive this function for the Airy disk and find algebraic decay in spectral log-frequency, implying the existence of arbitrarily fine spectral structure in the ideal, noiseless PSF. We use a differentiable forward model to numerically construct the spectral information eigenbasis and quantify the spectroscopic capability of diffraction-limited imaging across a range of noise and detector systematics. We demonstrate injection and recovery of the constrained spectral modes in a realistic simulated example and compare these results with previously reported methods. Our information-theoretic framework provides a generalisable method for spectral characterisation of PSFs spanning a variety of imaging contexts.

title: The spin-transfer inverse Faraday effect in Au/YIG thin film bilayers
summary: The inverse Faraday effect (IFE) (the generation of an effective magnetic field in a material upon irradiation with circularly polarized light) offers a pathway to ultrafast, non-thermal control of spin dynamics. title: Optical Quantum Memory Processing for Quantum Hashing
summary: Sender authentication is an important requirement for secure quantum communication networks. Bob's memory coherently maps the received time-bin photonic qudit into a single output mode according to phase encoding. Our scheme relies on a time-resolved coherent detection method introduced here, in which the coherent responses from individual time-bins are sequentially accumulated within Bob's spin coherence prior to the final sender verification. The key advantage of this coherent detection for quantum hashing is shown, and its potential applications are also discussed. The performed analysis demonstrates that experimentally verified parameters of contemporary optical quantum memories enable a proof of principle realization of the proposed architecture. These results reveal an additional role for quantum memories, serving not only as synchronization and repeater resources for long-distance quantum communication, but also as active elements for quantum hashing in conventional quantum key distribution systems.
